title.rendered: Our Father in Heaven | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 2

excerpt.rendered: In Aramaic, Abba was the word a Jewish toddler used for a father. Jesus authorised His disciples to use that word when addressing the Creator of the universe.

content.rendered:
In Aramaic, the language Jesus spoke every day, there was a word a toddler used for a father. Not the formal “father.” The intimate, trusting, dependent word. Abba. Jesus authorised His disciples to use that word when they addressed the Creator of the universe.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, October 4, 2026 | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 2

Today’s Scripture

“In this manner, therefore, pray: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name.”
Matthew 6:9 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

The disciples came to Jesus one day with a request. “Lord, teach us to pray” (Luke 11:1). It was not a casual question. They had grown up in a Jewish tradition where prayer was taken seriously, where the Shema was prayed morning and evening, where every rabbi taught his disciples set forms of prayer. They had seen Jesus pray through the night. They had watched Him come out of hours alone with the Father with authority that commanded demons and raised the dead. They wanted what He had. His answer was the shortest and most profound prayer tutorial ever given. He taught them to begin with two words that redefined every prayer the human race had ever prayed. “Our Father.”

In Aramaic, the language Jesus actually spoke, the word was Abba. It was the first word a Jewish toddler learned. It was the word a child used when they ran to their father in the courtyard. It carried intimacy, trust, dependence, affection, and the certain knowledge of belonging. No rabbi in Judaism had ever authorised the use of that word for the Almighty God. God was addressed as King, as Lord, as the Holy One of Israel, as the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. He was not addressed as Abba. Until Jesus. Jesus taught His disciples that the first thing they needed to know about prayer was Who they were praying to. Not a distant deity to be appeased. Not a bureaucrat to be persuaded. A Father who had already chosen them, already loved them, and was already leaning in to listen.

The Passion Translation renders Matthew 6:9 with the warmth of the Aramaic: “Our Beloved Father, dwelling in the heavenly realms, may the glory of your name be the centre on which our lives turn” (Matthew 6:9 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “Our Father Who is in heaven, hallowed (kept holy) be Your name” (Matthew 6:9 AMPC). Paul writes in Romans 8:15 that the Spirit Himself causes the believer to cry out “Abba, Father.” The same word Jesus used. The same intimacy Jesus had. Now extended by the Spirit to every believer in Christ.

How Jesus Prayed

The Format. Jesus began His model prayer by naming the relationship. Not by stating a request. Not by confessing a sin. By addressing the Father. The format itself preaches a sermon. Prayer begins by anchoring the believer in their identity as a child of God, not by rushing to the shopping list.

The Essence. Prayer is a child speaking to a Father. Not a servant petitioning a king. Not a stranger knocking at a locked door. A son or daughter walking into the Father’s room because they belong there. Every prayer the New Testament teaches rests on this foundational relationship.

The Authority. The authority to pray in Jesus’ name is the authority of a child who belongs in the Father’s house. The believer does not come to prayer trying to earn an audience. The believer comes with the standing already given at the cross. That standing is non-negotiable. Blood-bought. Spirit-sealed. Permanent.

The Assurance. A child who runs to a loving father does not wonder if the father will listen. The assurance is in the relationship. Jesus taught the disciples to pray with the same assurance of being heard that a well-loved child has when they call for their dad.

The Submission. “Hallowed be Your name.” Before the believer asks for anything, the first request in the Lord’s Prayer is for the Father’s name to be honoured. The believer’s agenda is submitted to the Father’s glory from the opening words. Prayer that puts the believer’s needs first has already lost the pattern.

The Result. The believer who prays from this foundation prays with both intimacy and authority. For Gospelbuzz readers today, wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, learn to open every prayer the way Jesus taught His disciples to open it. Address the Father. Anchor yourself in the relationship. You are not an outsider pleading for an audience. You are a child walking into the Father’s house. Pray from there.

Prayer (Pattern After Jesus)

Address. Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name. Abba. I come to You as Your child, bought by the blood of Jesus, sealed by the Spirit, welcomed into Your presence as one who belongs here.

Honour. Before I ask You for anything today, I give You the honour that belongs to Your name. Be glorified in my life. Be hallowed in my words. Be exalted in my decisions.

Submission. My agenda is submitted to Your glory. Let Your name be known in every room I walk into today.

In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am a child of the Father. I pray with the intimacy of Abba and the authority of belonging. The Father hears me because I am His. His name is hallowed in my life today.
